head_commit.message:
Make `bullet demo` work without a working directory or an env var.

Running `bullet demo` from a directory with no `target/` failed with
"SQLite path contains an empty or non-normal component", which reads as a
corrupt install rather than a missing variable. Two causes.

The default data directory was the relative `./target/demo`, so where it
resolved depended on where you stood. Default to an absolute private path
under the user's state directory instead; BULLET_DATA_DIR still wins.

And `demo` created that directory with `create_dir_all`, which applies the
umask, so a default 002 left it group-writable and the ledger correctly
refused it for custody. Create it the same private way `farm init` already
does.

`bullet demo` now runs from anywhere with no environment set.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
Paint colours the terminal can actually render, and keep the hints visible.

The console chose colour on `NO_COLOR` alone and then emitted 24-bit RGB
unconditionally. On a terminal that does not advertise truecolor - a plain
`screen.xterm-256color` with no COLORTERM, which is the common case under
screen and tmux - the navy ground quantises to black and the amber chrome
lands on a muddy dark red. The result is unreadable, and it is what an
operator saw on a first run.

Pick a representation the terminal can render instead: truecolor when
COLORTERM advertises it, otherwise indexed ANSI with the ground left to the
terminal so the console sits in the operator's own theme. NO_COLOR still
wins and still paints every cell Reset.

Separately, the bottom bar replaced the key hints with the error text, so
the one line telling you which keys exist disappeared exactly when you most
needed it. Show the error above the hints rather than instead of them.

head_commit.message:
Document how to actually run and use Bullet.

The README opened on a source build and a simulator demo, which answers
"how do I prove this checkout" and not "how do I use this". Someone who
runs `bullet tui` first had no way to learn what the panes are, which keys
do anything, or why the screen is empty.

Adds an operator tutorial: prerequisites, starting the console,
authenticating without putting a token in argv, the full TUI keymap, what
each view reads, the web Portal, and how to seed a ledger so the views are
not empty.

It also states plainly what does not work yet - submissions are accepted
and then settle UNKNOWN, and neither surface can approve, retry or cancel
- and carries a troubleshooting table for the refusals a first run
actually produces.

asserts that an unknown surface is inert, so the count now tracks the list.

head_commit.message:
Make the dogfood-on-bulletfarm run reproducible, and pay its receipt

Four gaps found by recording the run rather than describing it.

The Runner drove a real, billed turn and wrote nothing. `--dogfood-receipt`
was accepted and ignored, because the adapter composed the turn and never
called the evidence writer the CLI uses. An operator who spends real money
through this path now holds the same create-once proposal and receipt
whichever surface drove it.

The bridge seeded a one-file stub as the tree under review, which is all
the simulator ever needed. `BULLET_TXN_SOURCE_SNAPSHOT` seeds it from a
real repository's committed tree instead, so a real provider reads real
source under containment; that is how the recorded run read 1,867 files of
this kernel. Only the committed tree is copied, via `git archive`, so a
dirty member cannot leak into a run, and the snapshot repository is never
written to.

`BULLET_TXN_OBJECTIVE` replaces a hard-coded mission string, because the
objective is what the model is actually asked to do.

Without a credential grant the contained provider starts, answers "Not
logged in" and exits after a wasted spawn, so at least one grant is now
required rather than optional.

Defaults are unchanged: with no environment set the bridge still runs the
simulator, deterministically, with no account and no spend.

head_commit.message:
Drive the transaction loop from a real model proposal, end to end

The offline bridge never passed `--provider` at all, so it silently used
the simulator. That is why every Candidate this project has produced came
from a canned proposal. `BULLET_TXN_PROVIDER=claude` now drives a real
contained turn; `sim` stays the default so the component proof remains
deterministic and needs no account, network or spend.

Running it produced the first Candidate in this project's history built
from a real model's proposal:

    turn_finished exit Some(0)      real claude 2.1.266, 127 s, $0.36
    patch_applied: 1 paths          production gitd applied the proposal
    gate_result exit Some(0)        the gate passed on the real patch
    candidate_prepared can_6ed5e39f...
    candidate_preserved 427b1fce...

Five defects were found only by running it, each one a refusal that
arrives after the money is spent:

- The adapter used the operator's `--workspace-root` rather than the
  Runner's clone, so the provider would have read an empty directory and
  returned a confident proposal about nothing. `start` binds the session
  to the clone and the Runner's per-turn ceiling narrows the operator's.
- Supervision was a hard 30 s, sized for a simulator that answers
  instantly. It killed a real turn mid-flight and blamed the Runner.
- No credential grant reached the sandbox, so the provider answered
  "Not logged in" in 837 ms. At least one grant is now required.
- The execution envelope hard-coded provider "simulator", model
  "deterministic", adapter "simulator-v1", and expired after a single
  15 s lease TTL. A Candidate produced by a real model would have carried
  an envelope claiming a simulator made it.
- The parser reported an authentication failure as "assistant envelope is
  not an exact main-session message". It now repeats the provider's own
  words, which is the difference between a shape complaint and "Not
  logged in".

The `num_turns` bound was also wrong: it compared the CLI's own turn
count to distinct assistant messages, but one message streams across
several frames, so a clean turn reported 5 against 3 and was refused
after billing. It is now stated against frames actually ingested, and the
hidden work it was reaching for is checked directly instead:
`subagent_stats.spawned`, `max_depth` and `queued_turn_count` must all be
zero. Net tighter, not looser.

CI: the source-scan lane greps with ripgrep, which the runner image does
not carry, so it failed with `rg: command not found` on the first run
this repository has ever had. Installed like gitleaks, pinned by version
and digest, with no package manager.
